timeline: Ch2: Elena Voss enters the archive records room and interacts with the archivist.
Ch2: Elena examines a battered box containing a burned ledger from Saint Orison’s Church, dated 1974.
Ch2: Elena discovers a perfectly preserved wildflower inside the burned ledger.
Ch2: She notices missing names and overwritten signatures in the attendance records from the week of the fire.
Ch2: Elena identifies a recurring official’s signature, always with a trailing 'V', sometimes Ada Voss, sometimes 'A. V.'.
Ch2: Elena observes a cryptic sideways cross mark on altered pages, which appears to have been added after the fire.
Ch3: Elena compares the 1974 burned ledger and a recent death register, noting identical handwriting and the same 'V' flourish.
Ch3: Elena links the soot-black signature from the vestry wall to Ada Voss’s handwriting.
Ch3: Elena observes a faint ring of ash on her wrist, possibly a sign or residue from handling the ledgers.
Ch3: The sideways cross mark appears on post-fire entries, sometimes shaky or nearly erased in soot.
Ch3: Elena deduces Ada wanted certain names remembered only by those who would look closely.
Ch3: Elena finds a half-erased entry where the soot signature survives but the ink does not.
Ch3: Elena proposes the names form a sequence, not a random code: those who see the soot are meant to act next.
Ch3: Elena requests photographs from the church fire and the council’s keys to Saint Orison’s, suspecting someone unlocked the vestry recently.

Ch6: Elena examines a century-old blueprint of Saint Orison’s Church, discovering a ghostly overlay in faded pencil: a spiral staircase marked 'EXIT OF FIRE' and an unlabelled rectangle x-ed out in red.
Ch6: Gideon warns Elena that breaking the seal will cause the town to burn again.
Ch6: Elena uses the council key, which is warm and smudged with soot, to unlock a concealed basement door behind the altar.
Ch6: Gideon mutters, 'THE BELL CHOOSES THE NEXT NAME,' as Elena descends into the darkness beneath the church.

A wildflower was found perfectly preserved inside the burned ledger.
Several names are missing or erased from the attendance records for the week of the fire.
A recurring official’s signature with a trailing 'V' (sometimes Ada Voss, sometimes 'A. V.') appears on multiple entries.
A cryptic sideways cross mark was added to some pages after the fire.
The soot-black signature from the vestry wall matches Ada Voss’s handwriting.
The sideways cross mark appears on post-fire entries and is sometimes shaky or nearly erased.
The soot signature can survive erasure attempts that remove ink.
The names in soot and registers overlap and may form a deliberate sequence.
Someone recently accessed the vestry, requiring council keys.
The blueprint of Saint Orison’s Church contains a hidden overlay: a spiral staircase labeled 'EXIT OF FIRE' and a red X-ed out rectangle, possibly a concealed chamber.
The basement door behind the altar is old but recently oiled, indicating recent use.
Gideon believes breaking the seal on the chamber could cause the town to burn again.
The council key Elena uses is warm and smudged with soot.
spice_progression: Physical confrontation and warnings escalate; discovery of hidden church architecture and ominous warnings; supernatural or ritual danger implied.
